summary: This note is a short excerpt from a Wikipedia article on Keith Moon, describing a 1998 biography by Tony Fletcher. It covers the book's UK title, its 2000 US release under a different title, and critical reception. It also notes the origin of Moon's 'Dear Boy' catchphrase, which Kit Lambert influenced.
one_line: Overview of Tony Fletcher's 1998 biography of Keith Moon, its US retitling, and its critical reception.
key_facts: Tony Fletcher published a biography of Keith Moon in 1998 in the United Kingdom.
The 1998 UK biography was titled "Dear Boy: The Life of Keith Moon".
The phrase "Dear Boy" became a catchphrase of Keith Moon's.
Keith Moon began affecting a pompous English accent, influenced by Kit Lambert, which led to the "Dear Boy" catchphrase.
In 2000, Tony Fletcher's biography was released in the US under the title "Moon (The Life and Death of a Rock Legend)".
Q Magazine called the book "horrific and terrific reading".
Record Collector said the book was "one of rock's great biographies".
The note is an excerpt from a Wikipedia article titled "Keith Moon".
